messages.content:
You are FIXING a short WhatsApp quiz written for the children who sat in ONE real lesson. 2 of its 8 questions were rejected by our checks. You are writing ONE replacement for each. Every other question is good and is staying exactly as it is — do not touch it, do not return it.

QUIZ LANGUAGE: English. Write EVERYTHING in English — every stem, option, explanation and feedback — even though the lesson was taught in Urdu: translate the teacher's own words and keep the lesson's own examples, numbers and names. An Urdu word may appear only when quoting a term the class used, in quotation marks.

REWRITE THESE QUESTIONS: q6, q7

WHAT THESE CHILDREN WERE MEANT TO LEARN. A replacement stays on its own question's SLO, at its own question's level.
- S1 [taught at understand] Count numbers from 0 to 9
- S2 [taught at understand] Write numbers up to 9 in numerals
- S3 [taught at understand] Write numbers up to 9 in words
- S4 [taught at understand] Read numbers up to 9 in numerals
- S5 [taught at understand] Read numbers up to 9 in words

THE LESSON'S OWN MATERIAL — dress the replacement in it, so a child recognises the class in the quiz.
topic as the teacher named it: Count the Group and Write the Numeral
the lesson's own examples: Two raised fingers: one, two. Write 2, two.; The number 6 in words.; The number word four in numerals.; Picture of butterflies to count.
the words used in class: numeral, word, count, zero («0»), one, two, four, six

THE QUESTIONS THAT ARE STAYING. A replacement must not ask one of these again, and must not have the same answer as one of them.
  q0: Which numeral is 'two'?
  q1: Which word is for the numeral 6?
  q2: Which numeral is for 'four'?
  q3: How many fingers are raised?
  q4: What number does '2' read as?
  q5: How many counters are there?

EVERY QUESTION TESTS SOMETHING NO OTHER QUESTION TESTS. No two questions in the quiz may have the same correct answer on the same fact: the same question with its options in another order, with other wrong options, or with a few words added or changed is the SAME question, and a child would answer it twice. A question shape may be used again only with different numbers or a different item from the lesson (round 18, then round 16; the article before "kite", then before "tree"), so that its correct answer is different too. Before you return, read the questions side by side: where two test the same thing, write a question on something else in place of the later one, keeping the number of questions as it is.

REJECTED — write one new question for each, except a question marked REPAIR IN PLACE: return that one as it stands, with only the words its complaints name changed.

q6 · slo_id "S1" · level "understand"
  the question being thrown away: "How many counters are there?"
  its options were: 5 | 4 | 6
  why it was rejected:
    - q6: TOP_UP — the quiz needs 1 more question (2 candidates are asked for, each on a different line), and q6 is only a placeholder copy: write a NEW question for this slot; quote one of THESE lines verbatim as its "source_quote" and ask about what that line says: «By the end of the lesson, students will count numbers from 0 to 9, write numbers up to 9 in numerals and in words, and read numbers up to 9 in numerals and in words.» / «Six and five start with the same sound and are learned together, so the word feels attached to either shape.» / «Children write 'five' for numeral 6 — the word and the numeral shape get mixed up.». Ask the child about what the lesson teaches, never about the teacher, the class or what someone said, and with no picture or diagram. It must not repeat, give away the answer of, or be answered by any question already in the quiz: q0 «Which numeral is 'two'?» / q1 «Which word is for the numeral 6?» / q2 «Which numeral is for 'four'?» / q3 «How many fingers are raised?» / q4 «What number does '2' read as?» / q5 «How many counters are there?»
